means: what the ENCODING says about addressing, recovered by compiling programs whose addressing is known and decoding what Apple emits. One thing varies per sweep

alignment.answer: NO SEPARATE INSTRUCTION was observed for a misaligned access
alignment.evidence: an int written and read at a byte offset of one, through a char pointer cast, emits the SAME opcode pair as the aligned access - 12682 load and 17229 store
alignment.means: misalignment does not select a form at this width. What this does NOT show is that the hardware permits it: the compiler was told the pointer was aligned by the cast and may simply have believed it, and no dispatch can check because the safety gate refuses these opcodes

base_plus_dynamic_index.answer: ordinary integer arithmetic into the index register
base_plus_dynamic_index.evidence: A[j + tid] with j loaded at runtime emits a load for j, then an add, then the indexed load - no fused base-plus-index form appears
base_plus_dynamic_index.means: the base-plus-dynamic-index rule a weight arena or a spill slot needs is just an add, which is the same path a constant displacement takes and has the same 8-bit ceiling when the addend is a constant

beyond_the_immediate.evidence: op10279 carries displacements 1 through 255. At 256 and above the compiler emits op10282 or op10283 instead, whose immediate this decoder does not surface as an operand
beyond_the_immediate.means: an 8-bit unsigned field is the bound on a single-instruction constant offset. A weight arena or spill slot beyond it costs a second instruction, which is the same ceiling the loop-counter work hit on the compare immediate

control.means: the field map wrote bytes for displacements it had not seen and Apple compiled the same ones. A map fitted from a sweep and never asked to predict is a description of that sweep

displacement_owner.evidence: at displacement 0 the compiler emits read_sr, load, store and no add at all; at any non-zero displacement an add appears between them. No operand of the load moves with the displacement, in any of six element widths
displacement_owner.instruction: a separate integer add, op10279, emitted BEFORE the load
displacement_owner.means: the load carries NO displacement field. A compiler wanting base+offset addressing materialises the offset into the index register first

displacement_units.evidence: displacement 1, 2, 4 and 8 encode as immediate 1, 2, 4 and 8 for char, short, half, int, float and long alike - six element widths from one byte to eight, with the same immediate
displacement_units.means: the element scale is not in the add; it is implied by the LOAD opcode

element_width_selects_the_opcode.means: char, short and half share one load/store pair, int and float another, long a third. The width is chosen by the OPCODE rather than carried in a field, so a heterogeneous arena needs a different instruction per element width, not a different operand

index_width.answer: a 64-bit index selects a DIFFERENT load form
index_width.evidence: a uint index emits op12682; the same access with a ulong index emits op12688, preceded by a shl/shl.hi pair that scales the 64-bit value
index_width.means: index width is in the OPCODE, like element width, and a 64-bit index also costs an explicit two-instruction shift to scale. A compiler indexing a large arena pays both

negative_displacement.answer: NOT OBSERVED, and not shown to be impossible
negative_displacement.evidence: every negative source displacement tried compiled to a program with no add at all - the compiler folds it elsewhere - so this instrument saw no negative immediate to read
negative_displacement.means: the field is reported as UNSIGNED because 0 to 255 is what was observed. Whether the silicon reads it as signed is a question about a value Apple never emitted here, which only an authored dispatch could settle - and the safety gate refuses these opcodes

vector_width.answer: a four-wide vector access has its own form
vector_width.evidence: int4 emits op12709 and op17256 where int emits op12682 and op17229
vector_width.means: vector width selects the opcode as element width does, so a 128-bit access is one instruction rather than four

base_plus_dynamic_index.source:
uint j = C[0];
    C[tid] = A[j + tid];

threadgroup_displacement.int.label: tgdisp
threadgroup_displacement.int.note: threadgroup address space, which uses its own load and store opcodes

what_this_is_not: not a claim about what the silicon does with a displacement Apple never emits. A compiler-selected pattern is evidence that an encoding EXISTS, never that it is the only legal one, and every statement here is about the encoding
why_not_dispatched: g17safe refuses every load, store and atomic opcode as MayLoad/memory. That gate exists because two GPU hangs on this machine came from memory instructions, one of them taking the window server, so the authored oracle cannot ask these forms anything and this is not a queue to work through
